{{Quote|The Force can be bent to your will, but often there is a cost. The most powerful rituals of the dark side exact a toll few are willing to pay.|An unnamed Sith Master of the Dromund Kaas Sith Academy|<ref name="Revan" />}}
Traditionally, '''Sith sorcery''', also known as '''Sith magic''', was an arcane expression of [[The Force/Legends|Force]] [[Force power/Legends|ability]] first developed and practiced by the original [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] species through which they manipulated the power of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. The very name of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] was adopted by the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Exiles]] of the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]], who combined Sith mysticism with their own experiments into dark-side power to create even more strange rituals and [[Sith alchemy/Legends|alchemical sciences]]. Sith sorcery, while as much a part of the dark side as endowments like [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], was usually assumed to be accessible or at least within the mastery of only to those [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]] who possessed an intrinsic relationship with the more "magical" part of the dark side. Through the recitation of spells, execution of hand gestures, and/or the handling of [[Sith artifact/Legends|various artifacts]], [[darksider]]s were able to channel the raw power of the Force's malignant side to [[Qâzoi Kyantuska|warp minds]], alter the environment, and [[Force blast|obliterate]] whatever obstacles stood in their way. [[Gender/Legends|Males]] who achieved mastery were known as [[Sith sorcerer]]s, mages, magicians, or wizards, while females who practiced Sith sorcery were referred to as Sith sorceresses or [[Witch/Legends|witches]].

Sith sorcery was prevalent among the citizens of the ancient [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], and its disciplines were adhered to throughout the span of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|history]], predating even the [[25,053 BBY|inception]] of the longstanding [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Its effectiveness in battle was realized during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] of [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], up to and beyond the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] a [[4000 BBY/Legends|thousand years later]]. Lords and [[Sith Inquisitor|Inquisitors]] of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] were armed with Sith sorcery during the [[Great Galactic War]] of [[3681 BBY]]. Proponents of Sith sorcery revived its practice briefly during the [[New Sith Wars]], but it became something of an oddity following the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|reformation]] of the Republic in [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]]. By then, a [[Darth Zannah/Legends|lone]] [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] was its only active student. Still, the allure of Sith sorcery survived through [[Clone Wars/Legends|the fall]] of the Republic in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] and the subsequent [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], and curious Force-sensitives learned to harness its power from obscure temples on long-forgotten [[Planet/Legends|planets]] and [[Moon/Legends|moons]]. By [[137 ABY]], the sorcery of the Sith was studied by the foremost [[loremaster]]s of [[Darth Krayt]]'s [[One Sith]] Order.

==Description==
===Nature===
{{Quote|It's an innate gift.|[[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Darth Tenebrous]]|<ref name="SWDP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>}}
By those against whom it was used, Sith sorcery, also called [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Magic/Legends|magic]], was described as the full destructive power of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="Req">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: Requiem for a Rogue]]''</ref> Its strength was derived from negative emotions,<ref name="DSS" /> and grew stronger and more corrupting with each expression.<ref name="DLOTS1" /> Sith sorcery was every bit a part of the dark side as conventional [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]],<ref name="DOE">''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]''</ref> and when the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Exiles]] of the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]] found [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] and conquered the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] species,<ref name="EGTTF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> they incorporated the sorcery<ref name="TOTJC" /> of the [[Kissai]] priests<ref name="KOTORCG" /> into their own mastery of the dark side.<ref name="TOTJC" /> [[Sith sorcerer]]s of later generations learned to combine their exotic spells with traditional Sith talents while in the midst of battle,<ref name="Tandem">In the [[Tales of the Jedi (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi'' audio drama]], King Ommin switched between Sith sorcery and traditional dark-side powers during a battle; Exar Kun did the same in the [[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]].</ref> but when engaged in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]], those who wielded [[Lightsaber/Legends|said weapons]] were often forced to divide their concentration between casting spells and their bladework.<ref name="ChewGum">Darth Zannah had to concentrate separately on either her spells or her lightsaber technique while [[Duel on Tython|dueling]] on [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] in [[Darth Bane: Rule of Two|''Rule of Two'']] and [[Duel on Ambria (980 BBY)|against]] Darth Bane in [[Darth Bane: Rule of Two|''Dynasty of Evil'']].</ref> The sorcery of the ancient Sith was a complex power that assaulted an individual's psyche in ways that were difficult to both comprehend and defend against. Only beings with considerable strength of will were able to resist its psychological effects.<ref name="DOE" /> Conversely, a Sith sorcerer's concentration was able to be interrupted by [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force users]] skilled in the art of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Battle meditation/Legends|battle meditation]],<ref name="TOTJA">[[Tales of the Jedi (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi'' audio drama]]</ref> and their magical creations could be undone by [[Force Light|pure manifestations]] of the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side of the Force]].<ref name="BWOO2">[[Tales of the Jedi 2|''Tales of the Jedi'' 2]]</ref><ref name="SBW">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/livingforce/lf20050901sithbattlelords|text=Sith Battlelords}}</ref>

[[File:SithMagicRipples.jpg|thumb|left|250px|To untrained Force-sensitives, Sith sorcery was sometimes seen as musical ripples of energy.]]
Sith sorcery was perceived differently by those who were subjected to its power. Some Force-sensitive [[Sentience/Legends|beings]] felt as though it consumed their life energy,<ref name="FNU2">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising'' 2]]</ref> while others became physically weaker and felt like all their strength was being siphoned.<ref name="TOTJA" /> Some sensitives without any Force training suffered from headaches while in an [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] permeated with the residual energy of Sith sorcery. Its power was enticing, and sometimes manifested as a musical undercurrent&mdash;beautiful to some, hideous to others&mdash;to lure the unsuspecting. Sith sorcery tempted the curious with what was believed to be limitless dark-side power, and such an opportunity compelled many to explore further. Each interpreted their experience differently; [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Dllr Nep]] described visually seeing it as the ripple effect of disturbed [[Water/Legends|water]],<ref name="Req" /> while [[Beast-Lord]] [[Oron Kira]] saw the sky above him literally become overcast with the power of dark side.<ref name="TOTJA" />

Those who practiced Sith sorcery found its power a viable means of bringing their goals to fruition. Members of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon's]] [[Naddist]] [[Sith cult/Legends|Sith cult]], many of whom were seasoned sorcerers, believed themselves to be indomitable so long as Sith sorcery was theirs to command.<ref name="TOTJA" /> Its power was used for a variety of purposes through a number of techniques, ranging from mind- and reality-altering spells<ref name="ROT" /> to powers that impacted the physical world directly.<ref name="DOE" /> Some sorcerers applied Sith sorcery during their endeavors to control life and [[Death/Legends|death]]. Despite the various reasons individuals aspired to learn the ways of the dark side, two common themes were found in all those who subscribed to the study of Sith sorcery: reaching their full Force potential and the pursuit of ever-greater power.<ref name="Powahh">In the [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 90|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 90]], Freedon Nadd looked to acquire greater power through Sith sorcery. ''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]'' states that King Ommin sought to reach his full potential through Sith sorcery. In ''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]'', Darth Bane tells Zannah that she will be able to reach her full Force potential through tedious study of Sith sorcery.</ref>

[[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] believed that beings with a true affinity for Sith sorcery were few and far between. To him, Sith sorcery allowed an individual to channel the dark side with maximum effect<ref name="ROT" /> in ways that he, even as the prophesied "[[Sith'ari/Legends|Sith'ari]],"<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> was unable to do.<ref name="ROT" /> Still, Bane had some skill in magic and was able to make a Holocron.<ref name="DOE" /> To [[King/Legends|King]] [[Ommin/Legends|Ommin]] of Onderon, Sith sorcery was only attainable after breaching a barrier that resided deep within himself. At the behest of his [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]] and forefather [[Freedon Nadd]], Ommin was required to abandon his fears and doubts, lest through them he was consumed by the power he sought to control. According to Nadd, Ommin was only able to penetrate that barrier after he had fully embraced his [[hatred]] of everything&mdash;including the dark side of the Force. Once he accomplished that goal, Sith sorcery granted Ommin an amplified [[Force sense/Legends|sense]] of his environment; he was able to influence the malevolent sensations of millions of beings and fill those unsuspecting individuals with a hatred that was not their own. Such an exertion of the dark side was not without its detriments, however. Mastery over Sith sorcery demanded that Ommin sacrifice motor control over his body in exchange for access to the unlimited power of the dark side.<ref name="TOTJC" /> Despite this, Darth Plagueis's understanding was that with study, will, and an attunement to the dark, even one without the gift could learn any Force power.<ref name="SWDP" />

===Fear of Sith sorcery===
{{Quote|Not all knowledge is pure; some is touched by evil. There are secrets that must remain hidden; forbidden teachings that should remain forever buried. There is a dark side to the Force. Unchecked it brings death and destruction. The Council of First Knowledge is sworn to keep this terrible power from being unleashed, but the influence of the dark side is scattered throughout the galaxy, as are the tools it uses to spread: ancient texts of Sith sorcery; amulets imbued with malevolent energy; tainted crystals that can corrupt the minds of the innocent. Sometimes these artifacts are discovered by accident, and they fall into the hands of unsuspecting victims. They become agents of the dark side, wreaking havoc across the galaxy&hellip;unless we get to them in time. We are trained in the handling of dark side artifacts. Some can be destroyed, but others are too powerful and must be safeguarded.|Jedi Master Obba, 980 BBY|<ref name="DOE" />}}
[[File:KunTombRobber.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Despite their best efforts, the Jedi were unable to prevent the curious from seeking out sources of Sith sorcery, like Jedi Knight [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]].]]
Since the days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]], Sith sorcery had elicited fear from the Jedi.<ref name="DOE" /> Members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Order]] actively pursued practitioners of Sith sorcery, and took painstaking measures to hide, destroy, or contain the objects that assisted Sith sorcerers in their conjurations.<ref name="HOTS">{{InsiderCite|88|Heritage of the Sith}}</ref> The Galactic Republic recognized the dangers posed by the Sith and their sorcery and so outlawed its practice by the time of [[3998 BBY]]'s [[Freedon Nadd Uprising|Naddist Uprising]]. The [[Tomb of Freedon Nadd]] on Dxun was one such location where the Jedi hid a storehouse of magically imbued Sith artifacts,<ref name="TOTJA" /> as was the [[Sanctum of the Exalted]] on the planet [[Odryn]].<ref name="Exalted">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic: Exalted]]''</ref> At the end of the [[New Sith Wars]], the Jedi [[Council of First Knowledge/Legends|Council of First Knowledge]] was tasked with the eradication of Sith sorcery, which included the protection, or, if necessary, destruction of sorcerous Sith artifacts.<ref name="DOE" /> Nevertheless, the prohibition was ignored, and Sith sorcery was the weapon of choice on more than one occasion for many who entered into battle with the Jedi and the [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] of the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic's armed forces]].<ref name="TOTJA" /><ref name="DLOTSA">[[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]]</ref> By the time of the [[Jedi Civil War]], which ended in [[3956 BBY]],<ref name="KOTORCG" /> the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] had passed legislation that banned all things Sith.<ref name="POD">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref> Prior to the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the [[anti-Sith bill]] had been rendered void, as the Senate had since introduced new laws that strictly forbade religious persecution of any sort, including adherence to the ways of the Sith.<ref name="ROTSN">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> Fear of Sith sorcery again began to trouble the Jedi by that time, as they suspected that the powers of the dark side were on the verge of throwing the Force into complete disarray.<ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>

In the waning [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of [[Golden Age of the Sith|their Golden Age]], some Sith feared the power commanded by the more prominent sorcerers of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Empire]]. [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow's]] forages into previously unexplored avenues of Sith lore and ritual were looked upon with scorn by his detractors, who openly challenged his idealistic ambitions.<ref name="GAOTS2">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2]]</ref> King Ommin, a [[Human/Legends|man]] in the lineage of Freedon Nadd, was at first fearful of the sheer scope of Sith sorcery in his early experiences with it.<ref name="TOTJC" /> [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Bane, a Dark Lord who succeeded Naga Sadow circa [[1000 BBY/Legends|four thousand years later]], was also wary of Sith sorcery<ref name="DOE" /> because he lacked an affinity for it. He nonetheless allowed his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]], to indulge herself in its mysteries, but threatened to destroy the [[Gender/Legends|girl]] if she attempted to use her charms against him.<ref name="ROT" />

Sith sorcery survived Darth Zannah and was practiced with much less exposure than previous generations by subsequent members of her Order, including the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] of the Sith-ruled [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]].<ref name="Req" /> By the time of the rise of [[Darth Krayt]]'s [[One Sith]] Order, Sith sorcery was studied by the [[loremaster]]s of Krayt's Order, showing familiarity with the names of past sorcerers like Karness Muur from having access to the works of sorcerers such as [[XoXaan]].<ref name="leg30">[[Legacy (2006) 30|''Legacy'' (2006) 30]]</ref> [[Darth Wyyrlok (III)|Darth Wyyrlok]] was particularly skilled with using Sith sorcery to create illusions and was able to overcome the famed sorcerer [[Darth Andeddu]] in a duel with them.<ref name="leg27" />

==Applications==
===Acts of physical violence===
{{Quote|The magic of the Sith is even more powerful than we thought! Not only can we create illusions, but&mdash;''"<br />"''We can ''blast'' our enemies into ''dust''!|Satal and Aleema Keto|audio=SatalAlema-DLotS.flac|<ref name="DLOTSA" />}}
[[File:SpontaneousCombustion.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A victim of Force blast]]
Battle often required Sith sorcerers to unleash devastating spells to vanquish their enemies. Potent [[Force blast|blasts of dark-side energy]] were capable of causing physical harm to sentients, non-sentients, and [[Force ghost/Legends|spirits]] alike. Sometimes the sorcerer's hand was burned, but the power of the dark side made them impervious to the pain. King Ommin used the Force to blast several Jedi during the Naddist Uprising,<ref name="FNU1">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising'' 1]]</ref> and the royal tutor [[Korus]], after having his tongue transformed into a snake and lips grafted together, was finally burned alive upon receipt of an inadvertent blast of Force energy from newly trained Sith sorceress [[Aleema Keto]].<ref name="DLOTS1" /> Then&ndash;Sith apprentice [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] mastered the ability after acquiring a [[Sith talisman/Legends|Sith amulet]], one that augmented his already-increasing dark-side strength to new levels. He destroyed the spirit of Freedon Nadd in this manner,<ref name="DLOTS4">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 4]]</ref> and later incapacitated Aleema Keto the same way, after the sorceress attempted to attack Kun with her own blast of Force energy.<ref name="DLOTS6">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 6|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 6]]</ref> When Kun returned [[11 ABY/Legends|millennia later]] to harass the [[Padawan/Legends|students]] of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] [[Jedi Praxeum]], a trainee named [[Gantoris]] was incinerated with the power still wielded by the Dark Lord's ghost.<ref name="DA">[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']]</ref>

Several Sith sorcerers<ref name="ICanDoItToo">The ''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]'' identifies King Ommin, Queen Amanoa, and Novar as individuals able to create bolts of hatred.</ref> possessed the ability to form iridescent [[Sutta Chwituskak|bolts of pure hatred]]. When hurled at their enemies, the victim suffered from extreme agony as the voices of a thousand wretched souls screamed within their minds. Others were able to weave [[Odojinya|lattices of dark energy]] to physically [[Torture/Legends|torture]] opponents, while simultaneously [[Sever Force/Legends|severing]] their connection to the Force.<ref name="TOTJC" /> Both Darth Zannah<ref name="DOE" /> and [[Sith acolyte/Legends|Sith initiate]] [[Kyp Durron]] exhibited an even more sinister demonstration of Sith sorcery with their [[dark side tendrils]], mists of pure dark-side energy in the form of tentacles that were capable of causing immense mental and physical pain,<ref name="DA" /> and even the instant disintegration of flesh and bone.<ref name="DOE" />

===Altering the perceptions of another===
{{Quote|Out of the dark well of night they came, creatures born to the coldness of space. Devouring planets, swallowing stars, and drawing all ships to their deaths!|An illusion spell|audio=AleemaIllusion-DLotS.flac|<ref name="DLOTSA" />}}
The domination of another being's mind and will was possible through [[Qâzoi Kyantuska]], a spell that gave Sith sorcerers dominion over other beings<ref name="SWDP" /> and compelled those beings into actions they would have otherwise not performed. The more steeped in the dark side the sorcerer was, the easier it became to subdue the independent thought of another.<ref name="TOTJC" /> Large-scale mind control was evidenced by [[Krath/Legends|Krath]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Satal Keto/Legends|Satal Keto's]] complete control over the pilots of his [[CX-133 Chaos fighter|Chaos]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] during the [[Battle of Koros Major]],<ref name="DLOTS2">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 2]]</ref> and Exar Kun's puppetry of the entire Senate assembly during the [[Trial of Ulic Qel-Droma]].<ref name="TSW3">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 3]]</ref> Many [[4 ABY/Legends|thousands of years later]], an aspiring [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] Sith sorcerer named [[Cartariun]] enthralled the aboriginal [[Irrukiine]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Malrev IV]].<ref name="Req" /> While searching for an apprentice of his own, Cartariun sensed and touched the minds of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] agents who had come to the planet, as well as those of the all-[[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] crew of the ''[[Starfaring]]''.<ref name="AITE">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/96/indexp2.html|series=Aliens in the Empire|text=Part 1: Hierarchy of Power}}</ref>

[[File:Girovusestheforce.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Girov Dza'tey kills Cartariun with an illusory hand created through Sith sorcery.]]
Besides direct control of another sentient's mind, Sith sorcerers were able to distort the Force perceptions of the Jedi by pretending to be followers of the light. This was done by creating a [[false light side aura]], usually for the purpose of mingling with those who would have normally had a negative predisposition toward dark-side adherents. Both Freedon Nadd and Darth Zannah were skilled in projecting false light-side auras, the latter having learned the skill from [[Freedon Nadd's holocron|the holocron]] of the former. Zannah displayed her cleverness with false auras of light while infiltrating the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on Coruscant in [[990 BBY]].<ref name="ROT" />

[[Mind trick/Legends#Force illusion|Illusions]] borne of Sith sorcery were lifelike astral projections that touched all of an individual's sensory perceptions. Some Sith [[Historian/Legends|historians]] speculated that illusions disrupted the flow of the Force to the victim's mind, causing them to perceive their surroundings in ways that they otherwise would not. Illusions ranged from the transformation of one object into another, to the sudden materialization of beings seemingly from thin air, to the disappearance of objects that were in the victim's presence mere [[Standard second|seconds]] before.<ref name="TOTJC" /> Even [[Computer/Legends|computer]] systems were unable to discern the fallacy of the phantasmal images, which lent further to the dismay of those against whom the spell was directed. Only through intense concentration on the Force was an individual able to separate truth from falsehood.<ref name="TOTJA" /> Naga Sadow was a consummate illusionist,<ref name="fall4" /> as was the Krath sorceress Aleema Keto.<ref name="DLOTS1" /> Both made heavy use of illusions in their respective campaigns against the Jedi and Republic,<ref name="ItAin'tReal">Naga Sadow used large-scale illusions against the Jedi and Republic in [[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 3]], and Aleema Keto did the same in both [[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 2]] and [[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 1]].</ref> but their projections were defeated differently. An interruption in Sadow's concentration caused him to lose control of his illusions,<ref name="fall4" /> and the Jedi [[Mind Shard|used the Force]] to pierce Aleema Keto's conjured deception.<ref name="DLOTSA" /> The [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Sorcerers of Tund]], an ancient order of Sith sorcerers, also specialized in the creation of illusions.<ref name="KOTORCG" />

[[File:Qwi_Xux_Headshot.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Qwi Xux, a victim of Kyp Durron's memory-rub spell]]
Aside from outwardly expressed illusions, Sith sorcerers possessed the ability to create hallucinations within the minds of specifically targeted individuals by [[Summon fear|summoning their worst fears]]. After performing a series of intricate hand gestures, a Sith sorcerer was able to reach into a sentient being's mind and call forth that which scared the victim the most. The potency of the spell varied as the sorcerer saw fit. The longer they poured the dark side into the spell, however, the more likely it was that the victim would be unable to recover.<ref name="ROT" /> An individual was able to survive if they possessed significant strength of will,<ref name="DOE" /> though if not, there was a great possibility that the victim would descend into utter hysteria. Freedon Nadd had the ability to summon the fears of his enemies, and it was from the study of his magic that Darth Zannah learned to do so as well. The victims of Darth Zannah's summon-fear spell were many, including her own Master, Darth Bane. Although Bane was able to overcome her trickery, others were less fortunate. On two separate occasions, those on the receiving end of Zannah's [[Witch/Legends|witchcraft]] were driven into an irreversible insanity.<ref name="ROT" /> [[Rokur Gepta]], a member of the Sorcerers of Tund, was also able to torture his enemies by creating terrifying illusions within their minds.<ref name="DSS" />

Those who practiced Sith sorcery often believed themselves to be above reproach, and held no compunction about violating the sanctity of another sentient being's mind.<ref name="noRemorse">Exar Kun believed himself outside of the jurisdiction of galactic law based on his proclamation to the Galactic Senate in [[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 3]], and Darth Zannah exhibited no remorse for either Cyndra's or Darovit's fate after causing them both to go insane in ''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''.</ref> With Sith sorcery, a sorcerer was able to tamper with the memories of another. "[[Memory rub/Legends|Memory rubs]]," as they were called, erased<ref name="TOTJC" /> or rewrote select recollections of any intended target. Sith initiate Kyp Durron learned to wipe memories from the spirit of Exar Kun, and with it violated [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Qwi Xux]] so thoroughly that her mind had virtually become a blank slate.<ref name="DA" />

Sith sorcery also granted its masters with the ability to conceal themselves within the shroud of the dark side. When performed by a powerful sorcerer, the spell masked a person's strength in the dark side, preventing their presence or those of whomever they chose from being sensed in the Force even by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]]. Another of the spells learned through study of the transcript from Freedon Nadd's holocron, the [[spell of concealment]], was mastered by Darth Zannah, who used it to great effect against the Jedi on multiple occasions.<ref name="ROT" /> Such was the power of Zannah's concealment hex that ten years after [[Confrontation on Ambria|fooling]] a [[Ambria strike team|team of Jedi]] on [[Ambria/Legends|Ambria]] with it, the spell violently repelled the Force probe of a powerful [[darksider]] known as [[Darth Cognus|The Huntress]] into the healer [[Caleb]]'s [[Caleb's hut|shack]].<ref name="DOE" />

===Artifacts, locations, and weapons===
{{Quote|Emperor ''Palpatine'' recognized this temple as a focal point of ''Sith magic''!|Cartariun, regarding the Malrev IV Sith temple|<ref name="X-Wing Rogue Squadron 18">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 18|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 18]]</ref>}}
[[Holocron/Legends|Holocrons]] were Force-activated teaching objects that held near-infinite amounts of information. Many sorcerers of the ancient Sith Empire fashioned their own holocrons to include the sum of their dark-side knowledge. Those who specialized in particular aspects of Sith sorcery included only that area of ritual within their holocrons. Because of this, no complete repository of Sith sorcery was included in any one source.<ref name="TOTJC" /> Others recorded their knowledge in [[Sith spellbook/Legends|spellbooks]], hoping to ensure the continued availability of Sith sorcery's teachings throughout the generations.<ref name="PassItOn">Sith sorcery was passed on to Aleema and Satal Keto by way of a Sith spellbook in [[Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising'' 2]].</ref>

[[File:TranslationTalisman-TFNU2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A translation amulet]]
Sorcerers also imbued their weapons with the power of Sith sorcery. Amulets that facilitated [[Talisman of concentration|concentration]], [[Healing amulet|healing]], [[Shield talisman|shielding]], [[Talisman of ensnarement|ensnarement]], and [[Translation Talisman/Legends|understanding]], all did so because a Sith sorcerer chose to bequeath a measure of his power unto them. A young man named [[Warb Null|Shas Dovos]] created a suit of [[Sith trooper armor/Legends|battle armor]] based on the designs included in an instructional tome he found on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. Infused with the power of Sith sorcery, Dovos was bound to his creation after being approached by the spiritual guardian of the compendium, who then decided to rename him "Warb Null."<ref name="TOTJC" /> [[Kaox Krul]], a Dark Lord allied to Lord [[Skere Kaan]]'s [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]], combined Sith alchemy and sorcery to reinforce his battle armor with dark-side energy, which afterward offered nominal protection from Jedi attacks by emanating a defensive aura around its wearer.<ref name="DShared" />

On planets and [[Moon/Legends|moons]] where the Force was strong, Sith sorcerers erected monumental edifices designed as focal points for their dark power.<ref name="FF901">{{FactFile|90|NAD 1-4|The Shadow of Freedon Nadd}}</ref> On the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] world of Ambria, a [[Unidentified Sith sorceress|Sith sorceress]] built a massive [[Ambria Sith obelisk|obelisk]] imbued with the power of the dark side. The sorceress was killed, however, after failing to contain the released energies of an ill-conceived spell, resulting in the [[Devastation of Ambria|devastation]] of Ambria's landscape.<ref name="CSWE-Ambria">{{CSWECite|I|26|Ambria}}</ref> Other examples of such structures include the temples on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], engineered to be dark-side fulcrums by the Massassi servants of Naga Sadow,<ref name="FF901" /> and later by Exar Kun's Massassi during the Great Sith War.<ref name="TSW4" /> In [[14,000 BBY]], pure-[[Blood/Legends|blooded]] Sith sorcerers built a Sith [[library-temple]] on the planet [[Krayiss II|Krayiss Two]] where they [[Meditation/Legends|meditated]] and performed experiments. Numerous Jedi were killed while trying to destroy the temple over the centuries, including Jedi Knight [[Vara Nreem]], who visited the temple in [[3997 BBY]]. She entered the building after reciting a Sith incantation to gain access, and was immediately descended upon and devoured by the spirits of many long-dead Sith.<ref name="ATFTDS">{{WEGCite|story=A Tale from the Dark Side|book=Tales of the Jedi Companion}}</ref> As the [[Beast Wars]] raged on the planet Onderon, members of the [[Iziz ruling family|planet's royal family]] hollowed out a section beneath the [[Iziz Royal Palace|royal palace]] of [[Iziz/Legends|Iziz]] in which the remains of Freedon Nadd were kept. [[Tomb of Freedon Nadd#Onderon location|The tomb]] was the heart of [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Amanoa]]'s power, whereto she retreated to draw upon the dark energies that lingered around [[Freedon Nadd's sarcophagus|Nadd's sarcophagus]].<ref name="BWOO2" /> The [[Ommin's subterranean fortress|subterranean fortress]] of her [[Marriage/Legends|husband]], Ommin, was where the king's sorcerous powers were the strongest.<ref name="TOTJA" /> Millennia later, after the Republic had been reorganized into the Galactic Empire, its [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]], a Dark Lord in the line of [[Order of the Sith Lords|Darth Bane's Order]] called Sidious,<ref name="ROTSN" /> discovered that the dark side suffused the atmosphere of the planet Malrev IV. He had a [[Sith Temple (Malrev IV)|temple]] constructed there through which he intended to channel the power of Sith sorcery.<ref name="Req" />

===Disturbing the natural order===
{{Quote|&hellip;The fleeing Sith care ''nothing'' for the natural order of the universe&mdash;Indeed, the ''Sith sorcerers'' believe the order of the universe ''belongs'' to ''them''. Naga Sadow considers the death of a ''star system'' a ''small price'' for his own survival.|From the [[Tedryn Holocron]]|<ref name="DLOTS1" />}}
At times, the dark side was visibly manifested in a planet's atmosphere when summoned through Sith sorcery. By summoning their deepest and most potent negative emotions, a Sith sorcerer was able to create [[waves of darkness]], energy that radiated outward from the sorcerer in a spherical aura and instantly demoralized anyone caught within its radius. Individuals noticed that the area around them<ref name="TOTJA" />&mdash;whether within the confines of a building<ref name="BWOO2" /> or outside in the skies above&mdash;became visibly immersed in absolute darkness. Thunder boomed<ref name="TOTJA" /> and was accompanied by a roaring sound<ref name="BWOO2" /> as the darkness spread. Anyone caught in the vicinity immediately began suffering from feelings of intense horror, pain, and bewilderment. Victims were tormented by whispers of the dark side that left them in a state of total hopelessness, and prolonged exposure robbed them of the will to fight. Jedi and other followers of the light felt stifled, as though their connection to the Force was being smothered.<ref name="TOTJA" />

[[File:DenariiNova.jpg|thumb|left|Sith sorcery causes a supernova|220x220px]]
Many Sith sorcerers cared little for preserving the natural order of the universe, and held no reservations about disrupting it as a means to an end.<ref name="WhoCares?">In the [[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]], [[Vodo-Siosk Baas]] talks about how the Sith, such as Naga Sadow, care little for the natural state of the universe and how the death of a star system was of little consequence so long as his own survival was ensured.</ref> Such was the contention of Naga Sadow, who used Sith sorcery to ignite solar flares around the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Primus Goluud/Legends|Primus Goluud]], effectively escaping capture or destruction at the hands of the [[Koros fleet]].<ref name="fall4" /> Sadow later [[Battle at the Denarii Nova|decimated]] Galactic Republic pursuers by wrenching free the cores of the [[Binary star system/Legends|binary]] [[Denarii Nova|Denarii suns]], causing them to go [[Supernova/Legends|nova]] and annihilating the entire [[Denarii system]].<ref name="DLOTS1" /> During the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], sorceress Aleema Keto was taught by Exar Kun to harness Sadow's [[Supernova (Sith magic)|supernova-inducing power]]. She made use of her new talent during the [[Battle of Kemplex Nine]], agitating all ten stars of the [[Cron Cluster/Legends|Cron Cluster]] into a [[Cron Supernova/Legends|stellar explosion]].<ref name="TSW4" /> The result was the formation of the [[Cron Drift/Legends|Cron Drift]], the devastation of the Jedi planet [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> and the death of Keto herself, who had not been strong enough to control the power she had unleashed.<ref name="TSW4" /> Prior to his rise to power, the Emperor of the restored Sith Empire performed a ritual that resulted in the creation of [[Sith Emperor's ritual|The Void]]: an utter absence of all life, and of the Force. The Void subsumed light, sound, and even color, an effect which turned the world of [[Nathema]] brownish-gray in appearance. Even a [[3950 BBY|thousand years]] after The Void was created, it threatened to discorporate Force sensitives who dared visit the abhorrent world.<ref name="Revan" /> When he later established his [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], Lord Vitiate perfected and performed dark rituals that ravaged the atmosphere of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]] and created frantic electrical storms.<ref name="HPDK">{{Holonet|planets|dromund-kaas|Dromund Kaas}}</ref>

For thousands of years, the world of Ambria was suffused with the dark side, a side effect of a complex spell performed by the Sith sorceress who had once resided there. Unable to contain the vast quantities of energy her spell released, the sorceress was killed when it went awry, and the entire Ambrian landscape was ravaged as a result. It was only after the arrival of a Jedi Master named [[Thon]] and his subsequent battle with the residual spirits on Ambria that the planet's darkness was checked, having been trapped in a [[Lake Natth|lake]] by the [[Tchuukthai]] Jedi.<ref name="TOTJC" />

===Healing===
{{Quote|I used the Sith magic to repair your nearly-lifeless body, pilot!|Cartariun, to Wedge Antilles|<ref name="Req" />}}
[[File:MagicHealedWedge.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Wedge Antilles is healed through Sith magic.]]
Sith sorcery also allowed sorcerers to expedite the convalescence of an individual.<ref name="TOTJC" /> [[Karness Muur]], one of the original Dark Jedi Exiles of the Hundred Year Darkness, delved into and practiced dark-side [[Force healing/Legends|healing]].<ref name="leg30" /> [[Rin Shuuir]], a sorcerer of the ancient Sith Empire, wielded a healing amulet with which he rejuvenated the wounded [[Sith Warrior|warrior]] [[Utris]].<ref name="TOTJC" /> Freedon Nadd used the dark side to mend Exar Kun's broken body after the latter had been pulverized by falling rubble within the [[Great Temple (Korriban)|Great Temple]] of Korriban.<ref name="DLOTS3">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 3|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 3]]</ref> These powers could be used by some to remove poisons.<ref name="SWDP" />  The injuries of [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], and those of fellow pilot Dllr Nep, were repaired through [[Cartariun]]'s use of Sith sorcery.<ref name="Req" /> Although healing through Sith sorcery was possible, returning the dead to life was not usually thought to be.<ref name="LTOTS4">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Savior]]''</ref> In truth, some extreme arts could bring back the dead,<ref name="SWDP" /> such as necromancy.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse" />

===Incantations===
[[File:Incantation.png|thumb|left|220px|Incantantions where often used in Sith sorcery.]]
Spellcasting was an essential quality of Sith sorcery, as its practitioners believed that giving voice to an incantation tapped the strength of countless Sith sorcerers long passed. Any that required vocalization were only scribed in the Sith language, and could only be recited in said tongue.<ref name="BOS" />

===Necromancy===
{{Main|Sith necromancy}}
{{Quote|Freedon Nadd, for years I worshiped your name. For a lifetime I served the memory of your dark power. Now, in the name of my husband King Ommin, in the name of his ancestor Freedon Nadd, ''I call down the power of the dark side upon these foes!''|Queen Amanoa, invoking the power of Freedon Nadd|audio=InvokeSpirits1-TOTJ.flac|<ref name="TOTJA" />}}
When a situation required a Sith sorcerer to utilize more of the dark side than they normally had access to, [[Invoke spirits|necromancy]] often granted them them power they sought.<ref name="BWOO2" /> However, sorcerers ran the risk of becoming the puppets of the spirits they invoked.<ref name="DSS" /> Queen Amanoa summoned the spirit of Freedon Nadd to assist her in battle against the Beast Riders of Onderon's wilderness, but his spirit abandoned her in the presence of the Jedi.<ref name="BWOO2" /> To further his own Sith training, King Ommin also beseeched the spirit of Freedon Nadd, which came from the [[Chaos/Legends|netherworld of the Force]] to complete Ommin's initiation into the ways of the Sith.<ref name="FNU1" /> Ommin also requested assistance from Nadd to combat the Jedi, but as it had been with his late wife, the Dark Lord's spirit forsook the king when Nadd realized that Ommin had failed him.<ref name="FNU2" /> Nearly [[3951 BBY|fifty years]] after Ommin's death, four Sith Masters also attempted to resurrect the spirit of Freedon Nadd, but were thwarted by the efforts of [[Meetra Surik]] and her companions.<ref name="KOTOR2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> A much safer form of necromancy was to merely [[Tsaiwinokka Hoyakut|reanimate]] the bodies of the slain as soldiers, though they would lack the mental capabilities they had in life.<ref name="BOS" /><ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref>

===Protection===
{{Quote|The walls are lined with stonework, covered in carvings Babbnod says are&hellip;well, I can hardly believe it, but she says they're some kind of protective magic. Sith magic.|[[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Naz Felyood]], referring to Korriban's Valley of Golg|<ref name="KPLS">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031002korriban|text=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls|int=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls}}</ref>}}
[[File:KresshGauntletProtection.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A magically created Sith artifact protects its wearer from all harm.]]
Sith sorcery was used for defense as well as for attack. Sorcerers, fledgling or seasoned, were able to conjure [[Aura of uneasiness|shadows of uneasiness]] around themselves that repelled any non-sentient creature within range.<ref name="DA" /> The vague sense of discomfort caused by an aura of unease also affected cognizant beings, stirring in them feelings of sudden sickness and debility.<ref name="FNU2" /> Sith sorcerers were also known to perform magical experiments on inanimate objects, imbuing them with dark-side power in attempts to ensure the safety and security of themselves or others. Sith Lord [[Ludo Kressh]] used sorcery in the creation of a [[Gauntlet of Kressh the Younger|device]] designed to protect [[Elcho Kressh|his young son]] from harm.<ref name="LTOTS3">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]''</ref> The gauntlet of Kressh the Younger was later obtained and wielded by a failed Jedi Padawan-turned-Sith acolyte named [[Haazen]].<ref name="KOTOR34">[[Knights of the Old Republic 34|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 34]]</ref>

The ancient Sith also used their sorcery to protect the things they deemed sacred. Such a spell guarded the entrance of the room within [[Tomb of Freedon Nadd#Dxun location|Freedon Nadd's sepulcher]] that hid his holocron.<ref name="ROT" /> In the [[Valley of Golg]] on the Sith homeworld of Korriban, ancient sorcery in the form of [[Sith runes|wall inscriptions]] was utilized in the protection of the tombs of deceased Sith Lords.<ref name="KPLS" /> The magically created armor of Warb Null offered him greater protection in battle,<ref name="FNU1" /> as did that of the [[Sith Marauder]] Kaox Krul.<ref name="DShared" />

===Twisting life===
{{Quote|Following a complex series of rituals, the individual to be raised a Sith Battlelord was brought to the brink of death. Some claim the prospective battlelord was drained of all blood, though no consensus exists on how the near-death experience was to be accomplished. Once the man (or, less frequently, the woman) hovered on the brink, he was removed from the temple chambers (most reports put the ceremony in an altar room) by the members of his regiment. For the next hour, the members of the regiment paraded past their leader, viewing his near-lifeless body. After the regiment had seen the battlelord, he was healed, brought back from the brink and made whole once more. The effects of this ritual were initially startling, even to the Sith. The desired effect had been one of cohesion. The obtained effect was much, much stronger. Evidence suggests that the ritualistic death and ceremonial rebirth of the battlelord created a bond between the battlelord and his troops, as well as among the troops. The precise nature of the bond remains obscured, but it is clear that the Sith magics drew upon the power of the dark side to create a near-physical linkage among the affected individuals.|An excerpt from Jedi Master [[Kei Loo Bross]]'s ''[[Speculations on Tactics of the Sith]]''|<ref name="AMA" />}}
As Sith sorcerers sought to bend the Force to suit their purposes, they delved into bizarre experiments concerning the manipulation of both life and death. Before the Dark Jedi Exiles arrived on Korriban and sullied the bloodlines of the native Sith species, a king named [[Dathka Graush/Legends|Dathka Graush]] combined alchemical sciences with his mastery of Sith sorcery to create an [[Army/Legends|army]] of undead monstrosities from the corpses of those fallen during one of Korriban's cyclical civil wars.<ref name="KPLS" /> Graush also worked Sith sorcery in tandem with the most advanced and available technologies to fashion a dark-side<ref name="CSWE:Heart">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' {{C|Under ''Heart of Graush''}}</ref> [[Heart of Graush|crystal]],<ref name="KPLS" /> one imbued with more than a thousand Sith spirits,<ref name="CSWE:Heart" /> with which he replaced his own [[Heart/Legends|heart]]. When Graush was [[Assassin/Legends|assassinated]], the spirits of his [[Korriban zombie]] army joined those trapped within his crystalline heart.<ref name="CSWE" />

[[File:PlagueAtWork.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Beings caught in the throes of the Rakghoul plague]]
Among those who later arrived on Korriban and proclaimed themselves the first Lords of the Sith was a man named Karness Muur, whose magical endeavors surrounded the extension of life, and the preservation of a being's spiritual existence even after their corporeal death.<ref name="leg30" /> Muur crafted a special talisman in which his essence was preserved, but allowed him to influence the physical realm when it was donned by a living Force-sensitive being.<ref name="SWV">''[[Star Wars: Vector]]''</ref> The [[Muur Talisman]] served another purpose as well: through Sith magic,<ref name="Woman!">In [[Legacy (2006) 29|''Legacy'' (2006) 29]], [[Darth Reave]] says, "You command ''Sith magic'', woman!" to Celeste Morne.</ref> it was able to transform non-Force-sensitive humanoids within its vicinity into [[Rakghoul]] [[mutant]]s, [[Sithspawn/Legends|Sithspawn]] whose bite infected its victims&mdash;Force-sensitive or not&mdash;with an incurable plague that slowly transformed them into rakghouls as well.<ref name="SWCF">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031002rakghoul|series=Creature Feature|text=Rakghoul}}</ref> Following his defeat in the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] and subsequent [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] on the [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin]] moon, Naga Sadow used a combination of Sith sorcery and alchemy to mutate the descendants of the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] crew members of his [[Starship/Legends|starship]], turning them into even more terrifying warriors.<ref name="YavinDB">{{DB|location|yavin4|Yavin 4}}</ref>

[[Darth Andeddu]], an ancient Dark Lord of the Sith who ruled over the planet [[Prakith/Legends|Prakith]] long before the New Sith Wars, based his studies on Karness Muur's life-altering experiments.<ref name="leg30" /> He perfected the ability to [[Essence transfer|transfer his essence]] into another vessel, thus achieving eternal life.<ref name="DOE" /> On Yavin 4, Naga Sadow used technology along with Sith sorcery to enter into a state of suspended animation<ref name="DSS" /> before it was disturbed by a [[Nautolan/Legends|Nautolan]] [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] named [[Eison Gynt]], into whom Sadow transferred his spirit.<ref name="PFTR">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 7: Peace for the Republic?|int=Timeline 7: Peace for the Republic?}}</ref> Many more also discovered the ability to refit their spirits with new bodies, some organic, others into machines.<ref name="Xferers">Darth Bane and Set Harth learned essence transfer from Darth Andeddu's holocron in ''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]''. Darth Sidious transferred his essence multiple times in the ''Dark Empire'' trilogy, [[Callista Ming]] transferred her essence into a computer in [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], and [[Darth Krayt]] revealed that he learned to transfer his essence in [[Legacy — War 6|''Legacy—War'' 6]].</ref> The Sith Lord [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] used the strength of eight thousand Sith Lords to perform an [[Sith Emperor's ritual|incredibly complex ritual]] of Sith sorcery that stripped all life from the planet [[Nathema]], granting him immense strength in the Force and [[Immortality/Legends|immortality]] as a result.<ref name="Revan" />

During the [[Battle of Yavin 4 (Great Sith War)|final battle]] of the Great Sith War, Dark Lord of the Sith Exar Kun used ritualized Sith sorcery to drain the essences of all of Yavin 4's indigenous Massassi, seeking to ascend into a bodyless being of pure power. Kun's own spirit was sundered from his body during the ritual, but the combined might of the Jedi's [[wall of light]] succeeded in trapping Kun's wraith within the walls of [[Temple of Exar Kun|his temple]].<ref name="DSS" /><ref name="TSW6">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 6|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 6]]</ref> He also used Sith sorcery to trap the spirits of the Massassi children within a [[Golden Globe]] for all eternity.<ref name="TGG">''[[Junior Jedi Knights: The Golden Globe]]''</ref>

In the early years of the New Sith Wars, a [[Zelosian]] Dark Lord of the Sith called [[Darth Rivan]] made use of Sith sorcery in the creation of his fearsome [[Sith battlelord]]s. The spell was perceived in the Force as a strand of [[black]] energy that unwillingly and inextricably bound senior soldiers to their subordinates, and caused severe pain the further apart a subordinate was from his or her master.<ref name="AMA" /> The Jedi discovered that the spell was able to be broken with a blast of [[Force Light]].<ref name="SBW" />

==Users==
{{Quote|A rare few have a natural affinity for the dark side itself. They can delve into the depths of the Force and summon arcane energies to twist and warp the world around them. They can invoke ancient rituals of the Sith; they can invoke power and unleash terrible spells and dark magics.|Darth Bane|<ref name="ROT" />}}
[[File:NagaSadowIllusions-TFotSE4.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Naga Sadow, conjuring illusions in 5,000 BBY]]
Sith sorcery predated the formation of the Galactic Republic, a democratic institution that served the galaxy for twenty-five millennia. Members of the Sith species indigenous to Korriban<ref name="EGTTF" /> pioneered and perfected these rituals by which they called on the power of the dark side, to a degree thought unreachable by ordinary sentient beings.<ref name="TOTJC" /> A group of sorcerers who were exiled from the original Sith Empire relocated to the planet [[Tund/Legends|Tund]], where they practiced their radical sorcery in total seclusion.<ref name="KOTORCG" /> [[Adas]], an ancient Sith king who died circa [[27,700 BBY]], was a reputed master of Sith sorcery.<ref name="end">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> Of the many Sith in Adas's entourage was [[Raspir]], whom the King employed as a court sorcerer.<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref> Dathka Graush, a tyrant who succeeded Adas more than [[6950 BBY|twenty thousand years later]], also had a flair for Sith enchantments.<ref name="KPLS" /> Roughly [[6900 BBY|fifty years]] after Graush, Dark Jedi outcasts from the Jedi Order conquered the Sith species, and incorporated the species' magical practices into their own dark-side rituals. The Sith Lord Karness Muur was one such individual who, through Sith sorcery, developed ways to extend his lifespan far beyond what was natural.<ref name="leg30" /> Around the time of the Great Hyperspace War, Sith sorcery was widely disseminated among the Lords of the Sith Empire. Ludo Kressh,<ref name="LTOTS3" /> [[Tritos Nal]], [[Marka Ragnos]],<ref name="DSS" /> and Rin Shuuir<ref name="TOTJC" /> were among them. One of the most famous of that era was Naga Sadow,<ref name="DLOTSA" /> whose studies into the nature of Sith sorcery were a cause for concern among his fellow Sith Lords.<ref name="GAOTS2" /> Prior to becoming Dark Lord, Sadow began to train another in Sith sorcery, a Human male named [[Gav Daragon]].<ref name="GAOTS4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 4]]</ref>

As Sadow engaged in the Great Hyperspace War against the Jedi and the Republic, [[Omen|Sith dreadnaught]] under his command crash-landed on the planet [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]]. Stranded on the [[Wild Space/Legends|remote world]], the [[Grand Lord|leader]] of the all-Sith crew, [[Yaru Korsin]], used Sith sorcery in his role as luminary of the [[Skyborn]] [[Deity/Legends|deities]] of [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] legend.<ref name="LTOTS4" />

Many sorcerers recorded their magical formulas in Sith tomes, scrolls, and [[Sith holocron/Legends|holocrons]], and many more learned to tap into that ancient power through intense study of those artifacts.<ref name="EGTTF" /> Such was the case with Freedon Nadd who, prior to apprenticing himself to Naga Sadow, amassed a wealth of Sith knowledge from the holocrons of both Adas<ref name="end" /> and Darth Andeddu.<ref name="CSWE" /> In the tradition of the Dark Lords who preceded him, Nadd recorded the sum of his sorcerous knowledge within the recesses of his own holocron.<ref name="ROT" /> His descendants, King Ommin and Queen Amanoa, both practiced Sith sorcery, and dispersed its power throughout their Naddist cult. Among its most prominent wielders were the royal advisor [[Novar (Human)|Novar]], and Warb Null, the guardian of Freedon Nadd's spirit.<ref name="TOTJA" /> The Jedi attempted to prevent the spread of Sith sorcery by entombing Nadd's remains and his abundance of Sith relics in an impregnable tomb on [[Dxun/Legends|Dxun]], Onderon's fourth moon, but were unsuccessful.<ref name="EGTTF" /> Despite the Jedi Order's best efforts, Nadd trained two aspiring Sith, Aleema Keto and her cousin Satal, in the ways of Sith sorcery, and both became powerful sorcerers under Nadd's guidance.<ref name="DLOTSA" /> Sith sorcery was then spread throughout the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Empress Teta star system]] by way of the Krath organization, whose knowledge came from ancient texts and antiquities<ref name="EGTTF" /> gifted to the Ketos by the ghost of Freedon Nadd himself.<ref name="FNU2" /> Nadd also took another as his apprentice, the fallen Jedi Exar Kun, whose aptitude with Sith sorcery far exceeded Nadd's expectations.<ref name="DLOTS4" /> After inheriting Nadd's position as Dark Lord of the Sith, Kun joined forces with the Krath,<ref name="DLOTSA" /> and together they brought Sith sorcery to bear against both the Jedi and Republic in the Great Sith War.<ref name="TSW">''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War]]''</ref>

Exar Kun's [[Brotherhood of the Sith|Sith Brotherhood]] was ultimately defeated over Yavin 4.<ref name="TSW6" /> Sith sorcery had been temporarily defeated, but resurfaced [[3963 BBY|more than three decades later]] in the form of Karness Muur's spirit and his Muur Talisman.<ref name="KOTORV">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic: Vector]]''</ref> The same year, [[Celeste Morne]], a [[Jedi Shadow|Shadow]] working undercover for the clandestine [[Jedi Covenant]], acquired Muur's talisman<ref name="KOTOR27">[[Knights of the Old Republic 27|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 27]]</ref> and was given access to its magical ability to transform Force-sensitives into Rakghouls, a form of Sithspawn that transmitted their eponymous plague through their bites.<ref name="SWCF" /> Morne continued to wield Sith sorcery nearly four thousand years later, her lifespan greatly extended because of both the Muur Talisman and prolonged periods in [[Dreypa's Oubliette|stasis]].<ref name="SWV" /> Not long after Morne entered stasis for the first time, the Covenant's de facto leader, an undercover Sith acolyte named Haazen, revealed that several artifacts in his possession granted him the ability to command Sith sorcery.<ref name="KOTOR34" /> During the Jedi Civil War, the Sith Lord [[Darth Malak]] was known to have practiced Sith sorcery.<ref name="KOTORCG" />

[[File:Emperorreborn.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Sidious, a master of the essence transfer ability]]
During the New Sith Wars, the Sith Lord Darth Rivan made use of Sith sorcery in the creation of his fearsome battlelords. His servant, [[Darsin]], also possessed the ability.<ref name="AMA" /> Kaox Krul, another Sith Lord from the era of the New Sith Wars, practiced Sith sorcery and alchemy in tandem.<ref name="DShared" /> Roughly [[996 BBY|four years]] after the war's end, a twelve-year old named Zannah built the foundations of her [[Sith training]] on the sorcery of Freedon Nadd, which her Master had transcribed from Nadd's holocron.<ref name="ROT" /> She obtained other sources of knowledge over the years, and by [[980 BBY]], had achieved mastery over Sith sorcery.<ref name="DOE" /> In the centuries that followed, a fallen [[Anzat (species)|Anzati]] Jedi Master called [[Volfe Karkko]] abandoned his light-side path and (without any affiliation with the Sith Order or values) became an accomplished Sith sorcerer.<ref name="TSEUC">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030814trasaa|text=T'ra Saa}}</ref>

By the time the Sith Order to which Darth Zannah belonged had succeeded in [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|wiping out the Jedi]] and replacing the Republic with the first Galactic Empire,<ref name="ROTSN" /> Sith sorcery had become something of a rarity. Some Force-sensitives, however, like the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Len Markus]], became enraptured with the Sith teachings.<ref name="EYE">{{LivingForce|EndTimes: The Eye}}</ref> The Emperor, a Dark Lord in the line of Zannah's order called Darth Sidious, also studied Sith sorcery, and so did the [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adepts]] in his service. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Rokur Gepta practiced the sorcery of the Tund sorcerers.<ref name="DSS" /> Several untrained Force-sensitives, like the Imperial technician Cartariun, chanced upon the Sith temple on Malrev IV, where he learned to harness the power of Sith sorcery. A Bothan named [[Girov Dza'tey]] learned to tap into that same power through the [[Jeswandi]] [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]] techniques of his native people.<ref name="Req" />

Seven years after the death of Darth Sidious, the spirit of Exar Kun returned to terrorize the trainees of Luke Skywalker's Jedi Praxeum. He taught one student, Kyp Durron, how to control the Force through Sith sorcery.<ref name="DA" /> Kun was eventually defeated by Durron's classmates, his spirit was forever destroyed, and Sith sorcery again was left without any known practitioners.<ref name="COTF">''[[Champions of the Force]]''</ref> When the dark side was again on the ascendant more than a [[137 ABY|century later]] in the form of Darth Krayt's One Sith Order, the regime's foremost loremasters, Darths [[Darth Maladi|Maladi]] and Wyyrlok, studied Sith sorcery extensively.<ref name="LECG">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref> The spirit of Karness Muur and his living jailor Celeste Morne reappeared during that time, where they reintroduced the galaxy to Rakghouls and their plague.<ref name="leg28">[[Legacy (2006) 28|''Legacy'' (2006) 28]]</ref> The members of the One Sith recognized the beasts as the product of ancient sorcery,<ref name="Woman!" /> and all were destroyed along with their creators [[Battle on Had Abbadon|in battle]] on the world of [[Had Abbadon]].<ref name="leg31">[[Legacy (2006) 31|''Legacy'' (2006) 31]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I also thought it was time for us to get back to some of the mysticism in the ''Star Wars'' universe, hence Sith magic and Force powers.|Michael A. Stackpole, regarding the ''Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: Requiem for a Rogue'' story arc|<ref name="XWHB">[[Star Wars Handbook 1: X-Wing Rogue Squadron|''Star Wars Handbook'' 1: ''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'']]</ref>}}
The concept of Sith sorcery was first mentioned in author [[Tom Veitch]]'s [[Dark Empire endnotes|''Dark Empire'' endnotes]], a series of essays that explored backstories of characters included in the ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]], as well as those of several [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Tales of the Jedi'']] mainstays. While the endnotes simply referred to it as "primitive magic,"<ref name="endnotes">[[Dark Empire endnotes|''Dark Empire'' endnotes]]</ref> The [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Ulic Qel-Droma and the Beast Wars of Onderon|''Ulic Qel-Droma and the Beast Wars of Onderon'']] story arc of Veitch's [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (miniseries)|''Tales of the Jedi'']] miniseries was the first source to associate said sorcery with the Sith and the dark side of the Force.<ref name="Association">In [[Tales of the Jedi 2|''Tales of the Jedi'' 2]], Galia and Oron Kira reveal that Ommin and Amanoa command the power of the dark side. Amanoa later unleashes her waves of darkness spell, which the ''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]'' includes within the scope of Sith sorcery.</ref> [[1996]]'s ''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]'' explored further into the nature of Sith sorcery, explaining its relation to the eponymous species and subsequent adoption by the conquering Dark Jedi Exiles.<ref name="TOTJC" /> Sith sorcery continued to be used as an underlying plot device extensively throughout several of the subsequent [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Tales of the Jedi'']] story arcs.<ref name="SithMagic">Sith sorcery was used as the foremost of darksider abilities in [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising|''Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising'']], [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'']], and [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'']], as well as the prequel story arcs, [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'']] and [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'']].</ref> It was also featured in the cut ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' story ''[[Light and Shadow]]'', written by [[Paul Danner]].<ref name="L&S">"[[Light and Shadow]]"</ref>

Sith sorcery also served as a plot device in the [[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: Requiem for a Rogue|''Requiem for a Rogue'']] story arc of the ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron]]'' comic series. Storyline developer [[Michael A. Stackpole]] noted in the [[Star Wars Handbook 1: X-Wing Rogue Squadron|''X-wing Rogue Squadron'' handbook]] that he intended to revive a bit of ''Star Wars'' mysticism by reintroducing Sith sorcery in the ''Requiem for a Rogue'' series.<ref name="XWHB" /> It received recognition in the expansive [[Star Wars: Vector|''Vector'']] metaseries by way of the main antagonist Karness Muur, rakghouls, and the Rakghoul Plague, which were all associated with Sith sorcery.<ref name="Woman!" />

Several actions of the Sith Emperor of the resurgent Sith Empire fell well within the scope of Sith sorcery as described by sources such as the ''Tales of the Jedi Companion''<ref name="TOTJC" /> and ''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''.<ref name="DSS" /> The same applies for the ritual employed by the four Sith Masters in ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'',<ref name="KOTOR2" /> whose actions are synonymous with the description given in the ''"The Supernatural: Dark Spirits"'' section of the ''The Dark Side Sourcebook''.<ref name="DSS" />
